rubric.why: Identifies that an artificial satellite is made by humans.
rubric.description: States that it is a human-made object.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as man-made.

rubric.why: Identifies its motion in an orbit around Earth or another planet.
rubric.description: States that it revolves in an orbit around Earth or a planet.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the orbital motion and what it orbits.

modelAnswer: An artificial satellite is a human-made object placed in orbit around Earth or another planet.
It revolves around the planet in its orbit.

items.followUp: What is meant by work done by a force? Write the equation for work.

rubric.why: Defines work in terms of a force causing displacement in its direction.
rubric.description: Explains that work is done when a force produces displacement in its direction.

rubric.why: Gives the mathematical equation for work.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct equation.

modelAnswer: Work is done when a force produces displacement in the direction of the force.
Work = force × displacement, or W = F s.

items.followUp: Define kinetic energy and state its S.I. unit.

rubric.why: Gives the defining meaning of energy.
rubric.description: Defines energy as the capacity or ability to do work.

rubric.why: Names the S.I. unit of energy.
rubric.description: States that the S.I. unit is the joule.

modelAnswer: Energy is the capacity to do work.
Its S.I. unit is the joule (J).

items.followUp: Define power and write its equation in terms of work and time.

rubric.why: Defines power as work done per unit time.
rubric.description: States that power is the rate of doing work.

rubric.why: Gives the mathematical equation for power.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct equation.

modelAnswer: Power is the rate of doing work.
Power = work ÷ time, or P = W/t.

items.followUp: Define pressure and state its S.I. unit.

rubric.why: Defines stress as force per unit area.
rubric.description: States that stress is force per unit area.

rubric.why: Gives a correct unit of stress.
rubric.description: States that stress is measured in pascals (N/m²).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct unit.

modelAnswer: Stress is the force acting per unit area of a body.
Its unit is the pascal (Pa), equivalent to N/m².

items.followUp: State the relationship between stress and strain within the elastic limit.

rubric.why: Includes the condition under which Hooke's law applies.
rubric.description: States that the law applies only while the elastic limit is not exceeded.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the elastic-limit condition.

rubric.why: States the proportional relationship in Hooke's law.
rubric.description: States that extension is directly proportional to applied force, or stress is directly proportional to strain.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the proportional relationship.

modelAnswer: Within the elastic limit, the extension of a body is directly proportional to the applied force.
Equivalently, stress is directly proportional to strain.

items.followUp: Why is atmospheric pressure lower on a mountain than at sea level?

rubric.why: Connects atmospheric pressure to the weight of the air above a location.
rubric.description: Explains that atmospheric pressure is due to the weight of the air above.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the cause of atmospheric pressure.

rubric.why: Explains the decrease in pressure with increasing height.
rubric.description: States that less air is above a location at greater height, so pressure decreases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the variation with height.

modelAnswer: Atmospheric pressure is caused by the weight of the air above a place.
As height increases, there is less air above, so atmospheric pressure decreases.

items.followUp: Differentiate between heat and temperature, giving the S.I. unit of each.

rubric.why: Distinguishes heat as transferred energy, rather than a measure of how hot a body is.
rubric.description: Identifies heat as energy transferred because of a temperature difference.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for an accurate description of heat.

rubric.why: Distinguishes temperature as a measure of hotness and identifies its S.I. unit.
rubric.description: Describes temperature as a measure of hotness or coldness and states its S.I. unit, kelvin.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for an accurate description of temperature and its unit.

modelAnswer: Heat is energy transferred from a hotter body to a colder body; its S.I. unit is the joule (J).
Temperature is a measure of the degree of hotness or coldness of a body; its S.I. unit is the kelvin (K).
